question: Should `openclaw/plugin-sdk/archive`, `openclaw/plugin-sdk/root-walk`, and `openclaw/plugin-sdk/secret-file` become supported public Plugin SDK contracts, or should bundled consumers use non-public seams instead?
rationale: The branch deliberately documents these imports and raises generated public API budgets, so merging selects a durable external-plugin compatibility commitment rather than only refactoring internal code.

options.title: Approve the three public SDK subpaths
options.body: Accept the bounded archive, root-walk, and secret-file helpers as supported SDK contracts and keep their documented exports and compatibility budgets.

options.title: Keep the helpers internal
options.body: Remove the public package exports and migrate bundled consumers through internal or bundled-only facades until a broader SDK contract is approved.

recommendation.title: Approve the three public SDK subpaths
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded archive, root-walk, and secret-file helpers as supported SDK contracts and keep their documented exports and compatibility budgets.

likelyOwner.reason: The current PR series defines the proposed public filesystem seams and their intended bundled consumers.
